description:
About the Scholarship

The University of Manchester offers an unusual doctoral route through its Postgraduate Research Teaching Associate, or PGRTA, scheme. Successful candidates combine doctoral research with university teaching. Instead of completing a conventional full-time PhD, students spend approximately 60% of their appointment on research and 40% on teaching. The full programme lasts approximately 5 years and 10 months. Successful candidates receive a combined teaching salary and doctoral stipend of £28,832 per year, while their tuition fees are covered. The programme is intended particularly for candidates interested in developing both academic research and higher-education teaching experience.

Available Research Areas

The department is interested in projects connected with areas including: space engineering and design; digital manufacturing; sustainable manufacturing; laser engineering; robotics; materials physics; structures and dynamics; biomechanics; welding and structural performance; nuclear fission and fusion; nuclear fuels and graphite; nuclear policy; nuclear thermal hydraulics; solar energy; zero-carbon systems; energy storage; and biomedical engineering. Applicants do not simply select a fixed project. They are encouraged to work with a member of academic staff to develop a suitable PhD proposal within one of the department's priority research areas.

Eligibility

Applicants normally need: at least a UK 2:1 honours degree or international equivalent; an academic background relevant to their proposed engineering research; eligibility for admission to a relevant University of Manchester PhD programme; and an offer for a PhD place before being considered for the PGRTA scholarship. Candidates already registered for an appropriate PhD may also meet the scheme's conditions.

How to Apply

Applicants are expected to: identify a suitable academic supervisor; discuss and develop a research project with that supervisor; submit an application for an appropriate PhD programme; state in the funding section that they wish to be considered for the PGR Teaching Associate Scholarship; and include a written statement explaining their interest in combining PhD research with teaching. The scheme operates through supervisor nomination. Candidates selected after nomination may then be invited to interview.

Important Deadline Note

The University of Manchester's official scholarship page states that applications for this round had to be submitted by 24 July 2026. Therefore, this opportunity should currently be marked as Closed rather than Open.
